what_the_audit_is.question: A signal that drives an expanding curriculum must (a) move with competence while applied difficulty is held fixed (ANCHORING), (b) respond to difficulty in the right direction at fixed competence (DIFFICULTY RESPONSE), and (c) respond to its own actuator with the right sign (AUTHORITY). The audit tests candidate readiness signals on all three.

headline_sentences_the_section_can_carry: Time-out survival is the only candidate that is anchored: rank correlation with training iteration +0.987 (min +0.985, max +0.992) across five arms at pinned lambda = 1.0, with 4.6 direction reversals.

The learned mismatch signal that drove the collapsing curriculum is not anchored: mean rank correlation -0.037, spanning -0.300 to +0.110 across the same five arms, with 19.2 direction reversals and 32.3% of its whole-run range still in motion during the last quarter of training.

The same signal has no authority over its own actuator: |r(lambda, gap)| <= 0.035 in the receipt's descent windows, -0.201 over iterations 5,000-8,000 of lucid_s4_rg@s8600, and in both collapses cutting difficulty made the gap worse (-8.0% and -2.5%).

Survival's own defect is that it is inverted and saturating: it completes 95.3% of its whole-run rise by iteration 5,000, and the two collapsed arms end at 0.985 training survival against 0.950-0.966 for the three fixed arms. It is admissible only measured at a probe difficulty above the current frontier and driven by a monotone actuator.
The three candidates fail differently and must not be summarised as one failure: the learned gap has no authority and the wrong sign, return is inverted, and survival is inverted and saturating.
hygiene_notes: Spearman -0.7343 (return vs frontier AUC, 12 arms) is a rank correlation. Pearson is -0.6095 overall, -0.5977 among the nine controller arms.
Seeds 8600-8602 influenced development. The five anchoring arms are all drawn from them, so the audit is replication, never untouched confirmation.
Iteration counts here are PPO/environment iterations at 1,024 parallel environments, not episodes.

The audit's anchoring test assumes competence rises monotonically over a run at fixed difficulty. That assumption is what makes 'rank correlation with iteration' a competence test; it is an assumption, not a measurement, and should be stated in the paper.
The two collapses are the only authority evidence. n = 2.
